messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'aurora-ded-3' experienced multiple node terminations (spot preemptions). Impacting ~2/12 nodes in pool. Pager routed to oncall. See metrics: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/pool/aurora-ded-3

sre-jordan: ack. I'm Jordan (oncall SRE). Triage start. Pulling logs and node state.

infra-lex: adding context — region eu-west-1, pool tagged 'dedicated:enterprise-elixirnet'. Node IDs affected: n-23, n-26. Host events show spot termination notice at least-sig.

eng-runtime-anna: I see multiple in-flight model evictions for smaller RNN and transformer endpoints. KV cache for some sessions dropped, causing tail latency spikes.

sre-jordan: customer impact summary so far: ElixirNet (tenant elixirnet, VPC vpc-elk-12) routing to aurora-ded-3. 15% request errors (502/503), tail p99 latency up 2.4x on text-gen route. Notified support.

cust-ops-elixirnet: thanks — can you confirm data isolation and whether requests are routed to shared pools? We need assurances.

infra-lex: short answer: data plane (VPC peering) remains on their dedicated VPC; compute may be rerouted within our dedicated fleet depending on fallback policy. We're going to avoid routing to hosted multi-tenant unless forced.

sre-jordan: mitigation plan (immediate):
1) cordon & drain evicted nodes to prevent new pods scheduling on spot nodes.
2) activate fallback routing to standby dedicated pool 'ded-standby-eu' for elixirnet only.
3) spin up replacement nodes from reserved capacity or fall back to live allocation from our dedicated reserve.
4) run smoke tests and verify KV cache warm-up.

sre-jordan: running drain commands now:
```
rbcli node cordon --node n-23 --pool aurora-ded-3
rbcli node drain --node n-23 --pool aurora-ded-3 --grace 30s
```

ops-bot: ACTION: node n-23 marked cordoned by sre-jordan at 02:14 UTC. Drain initiated.

infra-lex: I'm preparing the fallback traffic policy. Will apply a tenant-scoped routing override so only elixirnet moves to ded-standby-eu (no multi-tenant exposure).

eng-runtime-anna: recommend temporary model downgrade for most latency-sensitive endpoints to the quantized variant (q4_0) to reduce OOM risk during reallocation. This is per-tenant config and can be toggled quickly.

solutions-ravi: I'll coordinate customer comms. Drafting status note: 'We've detected spot preemptions in your dedicated pool and are routing your traffic to a reserved standby pool. No data leaves your VPC. Some requests may see slightly different latency. We're monitoring.'

sre-jordan: applied routing override (commands):
```
rbcli route set --tenant elixirnet --from-pool aurora-ded-3 --to-pool ded-standby-eu --weight 1.0 --scope tenant
```
Confirming policy applied.

ops-bot: ROUTE: tenant elixirnet now has active override to ded-standby-eu (applied by infra-lex).

sre-jordan: spinning up replacements from reserved pool. Creating ticket to vendor to repro for hardware: "vendor-case 89432: investigate spot eviction frequency for aurora-ded-3".

dedicated-admin: ETA for replacement capacity from reserved queue ~4m for 1 GPU node, 12m for 3 nodes. I'll prioritize the elixirnet slot.

eng-runtime-anna: smoke test to validate routing + model variant:
```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  https://api.redwood.internal/v1/tenants/elixirnet/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium-q4_0","prompt":"smoke test"}' | jq -r .status
```
We should get status OK and latencies < 500ms median for small prompts.

sre-jordan: smoke tests running now. Initial result: status OK, 95% of requests hitting ded-standby-eu, median 320ms, p99 1.1s. Error rate dropping to 3%. Good.

cust-ops-elixirnet: thank you — can you share timeline to fully restore to their dedicated nodes?

dedicated-admin: replacement nodes provisioning in progress; expect full restore and rebalancing to original pool in ~25-35 minutes. We'll only move elixirnet back after KV cache warm-up and a canary window.

pm-maya: please ensure we capture a post-incident note with customer impact timeline and any billing credits as appropriate. Ravi — do we commit to a formal status update at 30 minutes?

solutions-ravi: yes. I'll publish an update in 30m with current metrics and next steps.

sre-jordan: short-term follow-ups:
- Monitor error rate and latencies for 60m.
- Keep fallback routing active until we confirm cache warm-up and p95/p99 stability for 2 consecutive 5m windows.
- Do not route to multi-tenant hosted pool unless alerted and approved.

infra-lex: creating internal postmortem ticket and tagging hardware vendor logs. Will include node-level metrics, preemption signals, and cloud termination traces.

eng-runtime-anna: we'll also correlate with model kernel memory patterns; might be a correlated KV cache pressure leading to eviction accelerations on spot nodes.

sre-jordan: handoff to next oncall (infra-lex) at 02:40 UTC for monitoring and vendor coordination. My notes for handoff:
- Actions taken: cordoned/drained n-23, n-26; routing override to ded-standby-eu for elixirnet; replacement nodes requested from reserved pool; smoke tests passed; customer notified.
- Remaining tasks: confirm replacement node health, plan canary back-migration to aurora-ded-3 once warm-up looks good, finalize vendor RCA.

infra-lex: taking over monitoring. Will escalate to vendor if we see >1 additional preemption in 15m.

ops-bot: NOTE: post-incident checklists queued. Reminder to open postmortem within 72h.

sre-jordan: tagging for follow-up: @eng-runtime-anna for cache tuning, @dedicated-admin for reserved capacity review, @solutions-ravi for customer comms.

cust-ops-elixirnet: appreciate the quick mitigation. Please keep visibility on any cost implications for fallback usage.

solutions-ravi: noted — we'll include cost delta in the update.

sre-jordan: closing my active shift. Leaving clear runbook in the incident ticket and the routing override will be removed only after explicit go from infra-lex.

infra-lex: acknowledged. Will post a final 'all clear' message and update the ticket when we rehome elixirnet back to aurora-ded-3.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: at 02:33 UTC error rate dropped to 2.1%, p95 latency back to baseline.

sre-jordan: thanks team. Follow-ups: vendor RCA, review spot allocation policy for critical enterprise pools (consider forced reserved or protected instances), update runbooks with per-tenant fallback steps.

solutions-ravi: drafting customer postmortem summary now; will share for review.

-- end of thread --
